attribution.note: Section heading in Zitron's own post, which he endorses. The Kedrosky quote below it is separate and not scored.

semantics.note: Read in context, 'best... will ever look' is a firm, open-ended forecast that the S-1 financials are the peak. The heading also bundles a separate claim about motive ('intentional'), which the proposition keeps.

contract.note: Zitron named no metric. Testing operating income and operating margin against the Q2 S-1 baseline is an ordinary reading of 'best', given his focus on profitability. The contract rightly treats the motive claim as a separate question.

evidence.note: Anthropic's own announcement confirms the S-1 was filed on Oct 26. It shows no later quarter and gives no evidence of motive.

reviews.rationale: No deadline was given, and the packet has no later comparable quarter that would trigger the early-contradiction rule. No finite record can confirm 'never'. Nothing in the packet shows the alleged timing motive. The forecast stays unresolved.

attribution.note: Zitron's own assertion. He presents the usage reports and Suleyman's remark as reported facts and makes them part of his claim.

semantics.note: The core claim is that both companies are in the top five, stated firmly ('undoubtedly'), and that both reportedly reduced use. The proposition leaves out the Suleyman June clause, but the contract covers it.

contract.note: Reading 'these large customers' as the top five for the nine months is fair, as is requiring credible reports of reduced use. Keeping internal use separate from distribution is reasonable.

evidence.note: The S-1 gives the top-five share (about 25%) but does not name the customers, so membership is not established.
Oct 6 TechRadar story, citing The Information, on Microsoft and Meta cutting internal Claude use. Supports the 'reported to reduce' part only.
June reporting quotes Suleyman's goal to reduce and 'ultimately eliminate' the Anthropic cost. Supports the June-statement part.

reviews.rationale: The reports of reduced use and Suleyman's June goal are supported (e2, e3). The central claim, that Meta and Microsoft are among Anthropic's five largest customers, is neither confirmed nor refuted: the S-1 does not name them. Nothing contradicts the claim, and the support condition is unmet, so it is unresolved.

attribution.note: Zitron's own sentence in his own post.

semantics.note: A compound claim: a numeric share of wealth, plus an overvaluation judgment ('hot air') and a remark about how critics are framed ('often'). Only the number is testable. The other two are rhetorical or have no measure.

contract.note: Using net worth as the denominator is ordinary. Requiring US stock-market equity rather than the Fed's broad category (which includes foreign and closely held shares) is a literal reading, if strict. The result depends on that choice.

evidence.note: Fed Q2 2026 data: $74.0T in equities against $195.9T net worth gives about 37.8%. But this uses a broader equity category and includes nonprofits, so under the contract it is a comparison only.
The Fed's definition of corporate equities includes foreign and closely held corporations. It shows the broad total overstates US-listed exposure but gives no isolated figure.

reviews.rationale: The broad Fed measure matches the speaker's 37% figure, but the packet has no figure for US-listed exposure alone, which the contract requires, so the number is neither confirmed nor refuted. 'Pumped full of hot air' has no valuation benchmark, and 'often framed' has no frequency measure. Neither can be scored.

attribution.note: Zitron's own assertion in his post.

semantics.note: Firm present-tense claim. The 'and/or' disjunction is kept, and so is the scope of 'largest customers'.

contract.note: Identifying the named groups from context and testing competing development under the disjunction is fair. Requiring proof that they are leading customers follows Zitron's own words.

evidence.note: Aug 14 Cursor post: SpaceX completed the acquisition, and the two jointly developed Grok 4.6. Supports that a competitor is being built, not that Cursor is a top customer.
Sept 28 Meta announcement of an enterprise platform with Muse Code. Supports competing development within the target period.
Microsoft AI says MAI-Base-2 was trained in Aug–Sep 2026. Supports competing development.
Oct 6 report of reduced internal Claude use. It gives no customer ranking and does not show plans to end the whole relationship.

reviews.rationale: All three named groups were building competing AI products in Q3 2026 (e3–e5). No evidence in the packet shows that they were among Anthropic's largest customers, which the support condition requires, and nothing refutes it either. The claim stays unresolved.
